name: Sill Line, Instrumented
tagline: Lit Sill Line with only its pictures redrawn: Status opens on an instrument panel (a named lamp board beside a moving-coil spend meter), every state lamp is one family of six signals with one meaning each, and the greeting's airglow is a phosphor halftone.
concept: A graphics mutant of Lit Sill Line: its colours, type and layout are the parent's. Three things are redrawn, as the dice rolled them. (1) Status's first read is an instrument panel: one thin graphite faceplate with two windows in the order of the page's own question. The wide window answers 'is it working'. It is a lamp board of three strings (Who answers, Keys, Connected), and every lamp is named under its signal in the tube's face. The round-shouldered window answers 'what is it costing'. It is a moving-coil meter drawn in SVG in the tube's light. Its scale is laid as the lineage's line, from a terminus ring at nothing to a T buffer at the day's limit, hatched from three quarters. The needle and a lit run stand at today's spend, and a bug on the rim marks a usual day of the last thirty. The legend is printed under the case, each signal once with its big figure. Past spending further down is print, not light: the cost table carries steel strip bars ruled at the quarters, and the same meter stands beside the words on the spending settings page. (2) Every lamp that says how a thing stands is one family of small signals, drawn on one 16-unit grid (static/sig-*.svg), and each signal has one meaning wherever it stands: a jewelled lit lamp, working (the only one that gives off light); a dot, waiting for its time; a ring, off or idle; a dashed ring, an empty socket, not set up; an upright amber bar, needs a look; a red block, stopped. The family reaches the lamp board, the legend, the boards, Settings, Worth a look, and To do's timetable on Home and on its own page, where a late task is the amber bar on the rail, a task due later a steel dot, and one with no time a ring. (3) One surface carries a texture: the greeting's airglow off the lit run is now a phosphor halftone, a dot screen graded by the light (static/halftone-*.svg), in place of the whisper of scanlines.
companions: The parent's, unchanged. Ink (#182536 plates with a #86a9cc cap) is what the family wrote. Steel (#58697a rails, #a7c4d8 links and the waiting dot) is the board. Pewter #7a8590 is the ring and the empty socket. Amber #ffb850 is only for needs a look: the upright bar, the late words and the setup edge. Red #ff6b6b is only for stopped: the block. Sage #86d9a6 is 'now' and done. #6dff9c lights only the working lamp, the meter's needle and its lit run, the mark, 'planning', Send, the box, focus and the tubes. On the glass the signals take the tube's strengths (dim phosphor for dot, ring and socket), and the bar stays amber so needs a look reads the same everywhere. Printed past data (the cost bars) is steel on a dark well, never light.
decisions: Rolled: an instrument panel (major), one family of small signals (minor), a faint texture on one surface (minor). Nothing else was changed. The layout moved only where the pictures needed room: Status's instrument row and the spending settings page's notice.

The panel follows the page's question in its order ('Is it working, and what is it costing?'). The lamp window is on the left and wide (it holds 13 named signals); the meter window is 22.5rem on the right. The two share one 3px graphite case with a 5px mullion of case between them and one power lamp. The legend runs along the foot of the case under the lamps it explains, and 'Change the limit' sits at its right end, under the meter it changes.

The meter is the lineage's line bent into an arc: a terminus ring at 0, 5% minor ticks, quarter major ticks, a hatched caution band from 75% and a T buffer at the limit. The needle has a hot core and the tube's two-layer halo; a lit run lies along the scale from 0 to today. The judges' fix for a needle resting at zero in stills (main round 12) is answered three ways. The limit is on the scale as the buffer. A bug on the rim marks a usual day, the last 30 days' spend over 30, written under it as 'A usual day: $0.04'. And the figure is printed large under the pivot. The drawing is fixed (src/dial_geometry.py); only the needle, the run and the bug move, by rotate() about the pivot and a dash on a pathLength of 100, so the template needs no trig. Near the limit the meter's window alone re-lights amber, past it red.

Named lamps: each string is one 44px link to its board (inverse when pointed at), and each lamp carries its short name under it (Chat, Digest, Lookups, Fallback; Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Telegram; Calendar, Weather, Web, Digest, Sign-in). The names of what is not working are set at the tube's dim strength, and needs a look is in amber. This answers every lens that asked, in round 2, for the lamps on the glass to be named. A screen reader hears each name with its state ('Chat working,').

One meaning each. 'Partly working' and 'needs a look' were two drawings in the parent (a half-amber lamp and an amber dot); here they are one signal, the upright amber bar. The Status row for 'This page' still using the installer's password now shows that bar, not a working lamp, which matches what Settings already said ('Needs a look'). The judges asked for this in round 2. So the tally is 5 working, 1 needs a look, 1 waiting, 2 off, 4 not set up, 0 stopped, and the heads' counts now read the signals (Connected to is 1 of 5 on the glass and on the board, where the parent's board said 2 of 5).

Only the lamp gives off light. The other signals are masks (CSS mask with the sig-*.svg shapes) filled with their one colour, so no glow can leak onto them. The lamp is a jewelled lens (a radial core and a lens glint) with a drop-shadow halo that follows the lens. Working lamps burn steady: in a signal box a steady lamp is normal. So the base sheet's breathing of every working lamp on Status and Settings is off, which also stops the harness catching them half-dimmed.
The zero rows the judges asked to drop or dim are dimmed ('0 stopped' in the dim ink at 400), not dropped, because the legend must show every signal once.

The halftone is a real asset drawn at the page's own pixel size (1px to 1 CSS px), so its dots stay round at any width. It is a 45-degree screen at a 7px pitch whose dot radius is the airglow's strength: 2.1px over the lit run, falling off upwards over about 60px and gone within 50px past the first stop, so the dates on the sill stay clean. The phone has its own portrait screen down the left gutter, where the run goes down. It replaces the parent's whisper of scanlines, so the greeting carries one texture only; the glass keeps its own scanlines (E14), which were there before.

Kept from the parent and the kit: the case, the spill, the tubes at screenGlow 1.0, the roll down each window on opening (one per window, hidden under reduced motion), and more-contrast and forced-colours rules for every new drawing: signals as CanvasText, the dial in CanvasText, the halftone gone.
title: What are we *planning*? (the parent's words, as a dice mutant keeps them). The household's own present tense: it asks what the family has on the go and invites them to tell Vera, and on this Home the lit line of plans the question stands on answers it directly below. The lit word is the job, not the motif; it avoids 'next', which the tube's NEXT UP claims beside it, and 'shall', which the judges found stiff. At 21 characters it holds one line at 40px on the desktop and at about 29px on a phone, and as the box's label it tells a first-time user what the box is for.
strengths: Status is now an instrument with a job: at a glance it answers the page's two questions in their order. Thirteen named signals show what works, and a moving-coil meter shows the day's spend against the limit and against a usual day. About 13% of the Status shot changed against the parent.

The meter speaks the lineage's language: a terminus at nothing, a T buffer at the limit, a lit run to the value. It is not a borrowed gauge, and its needle is the one thing on the glass that moves with the data.
The lamps are named on the glass, 'This page' says needs a look, and the heads' counts agree with the glass. These are three fixes the judges asked for in round 2.

One signal family with one meaning each holds on Status, Settings, Worth a look and both To do timetables. A late task and a setting that needs a look are the same amber bar, and only a working lamp gives off light.
The halftone is the phosphor's own texture ('glowing dots on the black') used where the light is, off the lit run, and nowhere else.
0 small targets on every page, smallest words 13px, no sideways scroll, and every hard check passes.
weaknesses: Outside Status the change is small at page scale: Home differs from the parent by about 0.4% of pixels (the halftone band and To do's bars), Settings and To do by 0.1%, and Chat, Ideas, Plans, the form and General not at all. A judge testing for 'nearly identical' will find it everywhere but Status.

Today's demo spend is $0.00 and a usual day is $0.04, so the needle, the bug and the terminus all crowd the zero end of the scale. The meter reads as 'empty', but its most expressive states (amber near the limit, red past it, a bug mid-scale) are not in any shot.
Status's words differ from today's by 21% (the parent's 9.5%): the thirteen lamp names, 'needs a look' in place of 'partly working', 'A usual day' and the cost table's share column.
The signals are small (14px on the boards, 20px on the glass). The dot, the ring and the socket differ in shape, but at the boards' size the dashed socket and the ring are close.
The halftone is faint by design and lives in a band about 60px tall under the tube, so at thumbnail size it reads as the parent's green glow. On a phone it is a column of dots in a 27px gutter.
The lamp window holds three strings in about 330px of glass, which leaves about 40px of dark glass above and below them.

Several states are still read from the rows' words in the templates (the parent's way): 'needs a look' for the installer's password, the short lamp names, a usual day. Each belongs in views.status_rows when it ships.
The six-signal legend is drawn only on Status. Settings and To do rely on the same shapes with no key on the page.
